chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Yazid al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Yaqoobi, on the authority of Isa ibn Abdullah al-Alavi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them all)

He said: Indeed, God, the One that has no substitute to be worshipped, when He made charity forbidden for us, He established the one-fifth levy for us. Therefore, giving charity to us is forbidden, giving the alms-tax to us is obligatory, and giving gifts to us is allowed.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْت: The Family of the Prophet, implied as the recipients in this context
key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: General charity, often given by those who consume it with impurity, forbidden for Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.الْخُمْس: The one-fifth levy, an obligatory financial duty for the community
key_terms.الْكَرَامَة: Voluntary gifts or presents, permissible for Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between sadaqah, khums, and karamah for the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal articulates the jurisprudential distinction between sadaqah (alms), which the Ahl al-Bayt are prohibited from consuming due to potential impurity (ghubsh), and khums, which is their exclusive right as a divine levy. It further clarifies that karamah (voluntary gifts) remains permissible, highlighting the Ahl al-Bayt's unique status as recipients of both obligatory and voluntary wealth while maintaining their spiritual purity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-53 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Yazid al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Yaqoobi, on the authority of Isa ibn Abdullah al-Alavi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali As-Sadiq (MGB), “I swear by God - the One that has no substitute to be worshipped - who made charity illegal for us that He has established the one-fifth levy for us. Therefore, giving charity to us is forbidden, giving the alms to us is obligatory, and giving gifts to us is allowed.”
